record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Describe all non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators that are reducible to several separate Volterra QSOs, in the sense that their dynamics can be decomposed into Volterra dynamics on component subsystems.

evidence.quote: Theorem 11. [38] The QSO constructed by the construction (18) with respect to measure (19) is reducible to q separate Volterra QSOs.
Problem 17. Describe the set of all non-Volterra QSOs which are reducible to several Volterra QSOs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ given by
$$ (Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy
$$ P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k}=1\ \ \text{for all } i,j. $$
A QSO is called Volterra if $P_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$; otherwise it is called non-Volterra.

Say that a QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ is reducible to several separate Volterra QSOs if there exists a partition $\{1,\dots,m\}=I_1\sqcup I_2\sqcup\cdots\sqcup I_q$ (with $q\ge 2$) and Volterra QSOs $V^{(r)}$ acting on the simplices $S^{|I_r|-1}$ such that, after a suitable change of coordinates respecting this partition, the dynamics of $V$ on $S^{m-1}$ decomposes into the independent dynamics of the operators $V^{(r)}$ on their respective coordinate subsystems.

Problem: Describe (classify) all non-Volterra QSOs on $S^{m-1}$ that are reducible to several separate Volterra QSOs in the above sense.
artifact.status_search_result: A full classification of non-Volterra QSOs reducible to several Volterra QSOs does not appear in the literature. Known results provide only specific constructions (e.g., non-Volterra QSOs built from product measures that reduce to $q$ separate Volterra QSOs) and partial studies of particular families/superpositions. Surveys note that the existing classes of non-Volterra QSOs studied to date do not exhaust the full set, so the general description problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: On a family of non-Volterra quadratic operators acting on a simplex
status_evidence.snippet: Studies particular parameter-dependent families of non-Volterra QSOs and their trajectories, indicating no general classification is yet available.
status_evidence.claim: Only particular families of non-Volterra QSOs have been analyzed, not a general classification of those reducible to Volterra QSOs.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Considers specific superposition constructions involving Volterra and non-Volterra operators on low-dimensional simplices.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address only restricted reducibility/superposition cases.

status_evidence.title: Continuous dynamical systems approach to analyzing QSOs
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that Volterra-QSO, F-QSO, and non-Volterra operators generated by product measure together do not cover all QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: The known classes do not exhaust all non-Volterra QSOs reducible to Volterra QSOs, indicating the problem remains open.
